newsitem.title: USA: Carrington sees higher overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Carrington sees higher overseas sales.

text.p: Cartlon Turner, president and chief executive officer of Carrington Laboratories Inc, said Tuesday the company's goal is to boost international sales significantly this year and to exceed 30 percent of its revenues by the year 2000.

"While 1996 revenues were primarily from domestic sources, the hard work of securing agreements to license, market and sell our products in 21 countries will begin to bring in new sales dollars in mid-to-late 1997," he said.
The pharmaceutical and medical device company said it posted a net income of $17,000 on revenues of $5.22 million for the fourth quarter ended December 31.
The results compare with a net loss of $1.006 million on revenues of $5.069 million for the comparable quarter in 1995, it said.

For all of 1996, the company said it posted gross revenues of $21.3 million compared with $24.4 million for 1995. Net loss for 1996 was $5.5 million, or $0.63 a share, compared with a net loss of $1.63 million, or $0.22 a share in 1995, it said.

It said about $1.4 million of the loss in 1996 was unabsorbed manufacturing costs that occurred primarily during the first half of the year. Those costs have been greatly reduced or eliminated, it said.
